slides.say: In JSX, most attributes are camel case. And class becomes className.

slides.text: JSX attributes become keys of JavaScript objects. Keys like these can’t have dashes or be reserved words.
slides.say: Why? JSX attributes become keys of JavaScript objects. Variable names cannot contain dashes or be reserved words like class.
So class becomes className, and stroke dash width becomes strokeWidth, in camel case.

slides.text: Exception: aria-* and data-* keep their dashes.
slides.say: One exception. For historical reasons, aria and data attributes keep their dashes, just like in HTML.
